title: RhetorLint contrast set
description: Minimal pairs for every rule: sentences that must be marked, innocent twins that must not, and strip probes whose output must keep every truth-bearing word. Each row records what the WORDS should get (expect) and whether the engine at this revision does (status). The data is engine-neutral: no offsets, so a JS, Python or Go runner reads it unchanged. test/contrast.test.mjs enforces this schema plus the rules it cannot express (the validator in test/helpers implements no conditionals): 'actual' goes with expect 'mark' and only with it; 'strip' goes with expect 'strip-preserves' and only with it; a known-defect row carries a tag; a priced-in row expects 'silent' and cites a file:line that resolves; text is ASCII unless kind is 'typography'; the file itself is ASCII, with smart punctuation written as \u escapes.

tags.description: One line per opportunity tag, saying which kind of fix closes its rows. The keys equal the row 'tag' enum.

id.description: Stable, unique row id. It never changes when the row's status flips.

text.description: The sentence under test. ASCII unless kind is 'typography'.

ruleId.description: The one rule this row is about. Marks from other rules on the same text are not judged here.

expect.description: mark: the rule marks exactly 'actual'. silent: the rule makes no mark at all on the text. strip-preserves: analyze(text).strip equals 'strip' exactly, so strip subtracts spin and never strengthens a claim or edits a quotation (for a negated or quoted intensifier, 'strip' equals 'text').

actual.description: Required with expect 'mark': the exact marked span, which must occur in text. On a known-defect miss it is the span a fix should produce.

strip.description: Required with expect 'strip-preserves': the exact strip output.

kind.description: What the row exercises. lesson: the tell used as the rule teaches it. innocent-twin: a sentence near the tell that should not be marked. typography: the tell spelt with smart punctuation. negation: the tell under a negator or a negative imperative. quotation: the tell inside quoted or mentioned words. named-agent: the source or doer is named in the sentence. unjudgeable-verb: a verb the words alone cannot judge. term-of-art: a technical or legal phrase that contains the tell's words. specimen: a real, attributed public sentence.

status.description: holds: the engine meets expect. known-defect: it does not yet, and tag names the opportunity that fixes it; when a fix makes the row hold, the test fails until status is flipped. priced-in: a false positive the repo documents and accepts, cited in 'cite'.

tag.description: Opportunity id from the motif atlas. Required on known-defect rows; it stays when a row flips to holds, so fixed rows remain countable.

reason.description: Why expect is right, in terms of the words, never the person.

cite.description: repo-relative path:line. Required on priced-in rows (the line that accepts the false positive); optional elsewhere.

source.description: Where the sentence came from: constructed (by whom), or the public document it quotes.
